keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1338-1343, before Cliopatria's first Chobanid shape. The Chobanids page: Hasan Kucek 'defeated the Jalayirids in 1338, paving the way for a Chobanid realm in the area around Tabriz'; the Hasan Buzurg page: 'Peace was declared in late 1338, Hasan Buzurg lost Azerbaijan to Hasan Kuchak and Anatolia to Malik Ashraf'. Neither page lists towns, so the 1344 outline is used as the nearest available shape; the extent of the Anatolian share is not given.

207,604 km2 for 1344-1351: Iranian Azerbaijan, Zanjan, Ardabil, part of Kordestan and part of Arran. The page's list ('Azerbaijan (where they were based), Arran, parts of Asia Minor', with Mesopotamia and west central Persia) is wider than the shape: no town in Asia Minor or central Persia is dated, so nothing is added. By the end of 1344 Malik Ashraf 'had gained effective control of the Chobanid lands'. The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: shape unchanged but valid 1352-1357 only; the years 1358-1362 belong to the Golden Horde and the Jalayirids

keyframe_review.note: The shape stands for 1352-1357 only: Chobanid rule ends in 1357 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1357'; 'forces of the Golden Horde overran the Chobanid realm and captured Tabriz in 1357'), but Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1362. For 1358-1362 Azerbaijan is Jalayirid (conquered by Uways in August 1358) except for the Muzaffarid occupation of 1359-1360; Cliopatria's Chobanids row should end in 1357. ledger.note: 1338: Hasan Kucek defeats the Jalayirids and founds the Chobanid realm around Tabriz. Hasan Kucek 'defeated the Jalayirids in 1338, paving the way for a Chobanid realm in the area around Tabriz'; infobox 'Established: 1338'. The Hasan Buzurg page dates the battle to 16 July 1338 at Naushahr in the Alatagh area.

Late 1338: the peace gives Azerbaijan to Hasan Kuchak. 'Peace was declared in late 1338, Hasan Buzurg lost Azerbaijan to Hasan Kuchak and Anatolia to Malik Ashraf.' The Anatolian share is not located by the page.

1339: Pir Husayn Chubani becomes governor of Fars and Isfahan. 'Pir Husayn Chubani was governor of Fars and Isfahan from 1339 to 1342' (the page gives the span, not the manner of the takeover; the Ilkhanate is the counterpart as the overlord whose governors had held the provinces, my reading).

1342: the Injuid Abu Ishaq replaces the Chobanids in southern Iran. 'the Injuid Abu Ishaq Inju in 1342, who replaced the Chobanids in southern Iran'; the Injuids page has him take Shiraz from Yagi Basti in March 1343.

wars.name: Chobanid-Jalayirid war of 1338
wars.outcome: Hasan Kucek beat Hasan Buzurg (16 July 1338, Naushahr); the peace of late 1338 gave Azerbaijan to the Chobanids.

wars.name: Chobanid attack on Baghdad (1347)
wars.outcome: Malik Ashraf's army failed to take Baghdad and retreated by the summer after heavy losses.

wars.name: Chobanid attack on Fars (1350)
wars.outcome: 'He also failed to seize Fars from the Injuids in 1350.'
wars.note: The Injuids page does not mention this attack.

wars.name: Golden Horde conquest of the Chobanid realm
wars.outcome: The Golden Horde captured Tabriz in 1357, executed Malik Ashraf and carried his family north.
wars.note: The Golden Horde dossier dates Tabriz to 1356; the page does not name Jani Beg.

certainty.note: No page gives a treaty line; the Jalayirid frontier at Baghdad and the Injuid frontier in Fars are approximate.

notes: Pages: two (budget 1-2). Start 1338 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1344; end 1357 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1362: the row's last five years belong to the Golden Horde and Jalayirids, and Cliopatria's Chobanids shape still covers Azerbaijan in 1357-1362 (checked on the gazetteer). The pages give no area and no list of towns, so shapes 1344 and 1352 stay as drawn; the page's wider list (Asia Minor, Mesopotamia, west central Persia) is unverified. Hasan Kucek's death and the date Malik Ashraf took over are not on the pages (only 'By the end of 1344, Malek Asraf had gained effective control'); no ruler list was extracted, so identity.rulers is omitted. The Fars-Isfahan governorship of Pir Husayn (1339-1342) is the page's span; the first event is therefore confidence 2. The Golden Horde dossier dates the fall of Tabriz to 1356, this page to 1357. The Jalayirid dossier starts in 1340, so the 1338 loss of Azerbaijan has no mirror in it; a gap-filler may choose to start the Jalayirid state in 1338.
